text.p: Caspian Securities said Friday it had upgraded Argentine steelmaker Siderar SAIC to buy from market performer after raising its earnings estimates for 1998 and 1999 by 13 percent and 23 percent respectively.
Caspian said it was increasing its earnings estimates to reflect the benefits from the acquisition in April of Comesi, a flat galvanized steel firm for which it paid $65 million.

"We believe the market has not fully valued Comesi's potential, in spite of Siderar's strong appreciation year to date, and we have set our 12-month price target at $5.50, implying upside of 22 percent," said Caspian.
The brokers said in a research note that Comesi would start contributing to Siderar's earnings in the quarter that ended in June.
